answer: Jurors whose votes correlate above 54% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the ember quorum in the lotus ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the violet history shows each cut. A farm that captures 71 seats as a result pays for 71 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 19 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
